capacity_utilization.note: ISSUER STATES NIL - this is the RHP's own affirmative 'not applicable', NOT an extraction gap. Verbatim, under the heading 'CAPACITY AND CAPACITY UTILIZATION' in 'Our Business' (RHP printed page 205 / PDF page 209): 'Our Company is engaged in media and entertainment services and hence capacity and capacity utilization is not applicable to us.' Corroborated twice: under 'RAW MATERIALS' in the same chapter (printed page 203 / PDF page 207) - 'Since we are not a manufacturing company, details of raw materials are not applicable to us.'; and under 'Capacity/facility creation, location of plants' in 'History and Certain Corporate Matters' (printed page 228 / PDF page 232) - 'Since our Company is engaged in M&E Industry, we do not have any product manufacturing facilities.' The RHP prints NO installed capacity, no studio / floor / screen capacity, no production-slate capacity (films or episodes per year) and no utilisation percentage anywhere, for any FY. Every other 'capacity' occurrence in the issuer's own sections was checked and none is a capacity disclosure: (i) the growth strategy 'Increase our production capacity' (printed page 198 / PDF page 202) is purely qualitative - 'we will expand our organization's sourcing and production capacity ... by hiring young talent, grooming them and building a creative leadership bench' - and attaches no number, no unit and no slate count; (ii) the Risk Factors mention (printed page 47 / PDF page 51) is about third-party exhibitors - 'there can be no assurance that occupancy rates at theatres in India or demand for our projects will not fall' - i.e. cinemas' occupancy, not the Company's capacity; (iii) the remaining hits are auditors/experts acting 'in their capacity as', a KMP acting 'in his capacity', and D&B industry-chapter text (pages 137, 146, 160) which is commissioned third-party material, not issuer disclosure. The Company owns no production facility: its only owned operating premises is an administrative office, and its other locations are a leased registered office and two leased storage godowns (see plants[]); equipment such as cameras, lights and grips is rented from third-party local players. Consequently installed_by_fy and utilization_pct_by_fy are correctly null - the issuer states the concept does not apply to it.

channel_mix.note: ISSUER-SILENT, verified - the RHP prints no B2B/B2C split and no distribution-channel revenue split of any kind, so b2b_pct / b2c_pct are correctly null. Search terms run over the full staged text (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed): 'B2B' 0 hits, 'B2C' 0 hits, 'business-to-business' 0, 'business to business' 0, 'business-to-consumer' 0, 'direct-to-consumer' 0, 'channel partner' 0, 'aggregator' 0; 'end consumer' 1 hit and 'syndication' 2 hits, all three in the commissioned D&B industry chapter or in the marketing narrative, none carrying a split; 'sub-distributor' 1 hit (box-office reporting risk factor). Also probed by the document's own phrasing - 'theatrical', 'theatrical rights', 'satellite rights', 'digital rights', 'music rights', 'distribution rights', 'overseas rights', 'revenue stream', 'revenue model', 'mode of exploitation', 'bifurcation', '% of total revenue', 'as % of revenue' - and no theatrical-vs-OTT-vs-satellite-vs-music revenue table exists for the issuer (the only theatrical/digital percentage split in the document, 61% domestic theatricals, is D&B industry data on PDF page 189 and is expressly excluded). What the RHP does say qualitatively about its routes to market, under 'OUR CUSTOMERS' (printed page 202 / PDF page 206): 'We generate a major portion of revenues from renowned studios with whom we co-produced our films and independent distributors whom we sell our distribution rights' - and elsewhere it names OTT platforms, broadcasters and its own social-media channels (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook) as monetisation routes, plus overseas distributors for export. The customer table on that page is a top-1/3/5/10 CONCENTRATION table (already in customer_concentration), not a channel split, and the RHP adds that it cannot name those customers for want of consent. The model is substantively 100% business-to-business (studios, distributors, OTT platforms, broadcasters and overseas distributors are the paying counterparties; theatrical receipts reach the Company as a share of gross box office collected through exhibitors and distributors), but the RHP never states a percentage, so no b2b_pct is recorded here rather than deriving one. NOTE ON WHAT IS NOT A CHANNEL MIX: revenue_split_product (films 89.68% / web-series 1.32% / others 8.99% for FY26) is a product-segment split, and the RHP's second table - sole-produced 90.00% vs co-produced 0.00% vs others 10.00% for FY26 (FY25: 78.60 / 21.38 / 0.02; FY24: 99.83 / 0.00 / 0.17, printed page 32 / PDF page 36) - is a production-model split; neither is a customer-type or distribution-channel mix. The only route-based percentage the RHP prints is export revenue (13.45% FY26, 0.04% FY25, 3.20% FY24), already carried in domestic_export_mix and revenue_split_geography.

business_ops.seasonality: Stated not seasonal, verbatim: 'The extent to which business is seasonal. Our business does not depend to a certain extent on the seasonal, environmental and climate changes. Hence, our business is not seasonal in nature.' The RHP nonetheless lists among the factors that may affect future results: 'Revenues from theatrical releases are subject to volatility due to competition, seasonality, and audience turnout, which can fluctuate significantly.' Revenue is instead described as lumpy and release-driven - a major portion depends on the box office success of films and on streaming deals with OTT platforms, and MD&A explains the Fiscal 2026 inventory-days spike to 1,328 days (from 173 days in Fiscal 2025 and 119 days in Fiscal 2024) as a consequence of the Company having released only one major movie/web series during the year.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Vertically integrated content originator rather than a manufacturer: the Company states it engages in 'research & development of scripts, end-to-end production of content, intellectual property creation, monetization of rights and distribution'. Production runs from conceptualization and scripting, through cast/crew finalisation, a cost-of-production budget covering pre-production, production and post-production, and a separate Print and Advertising (P&A) budget covering marketing and distribution. Editing is generally carried out in-house 'for creative reasons'; dubbing, sound and VFX are outsourced to different studios/professionals while closely monitored. Post-production capability is described as digital intermediate (DI) colour grading, high-resolution editing suites, Dolby Atmos sound mixing and VFX pipelines. Two operating models: (i) co-production with a reputable studio, where the Company produces for a fixed fee plus a share of the intellectual property and profits, giving 'certainty in earnings' and de-risking cashflows; and (ii) sole production, where the Company finances the entire project and retains all rights - intellectual property, titles and distribution rights - allowing it to keep the entire theatrical upside and monetise OTT, music rights and downstream derivatives (remakes, sequels/prequels, spin-offs, dubbings, foreign-language renditions, stage plays, web series and television production). Forward channel is via renowned studios, independent distributors, OTT platforms and broadcasters, plus the Company's own social media presence (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook). Backward integration is deliberately light: 'Since we are not a manufacturing company, details of raw materials are not applicable to us'; equipment (cameras, lights, grips, picture vehicles, setting equipment) is rented from third-party local players, while the Company uses its own editing equipment; power is drawn from the local grid supplemented by hired diesel generator sets at shooting sites; water is required only for drinking and sanitary purposes. Cost control measures include a no-cash / minimum-cash payment policy with payments through banking channels and on-set accountants to manage payments, track daily expenses and audit. The Company states it has not entered into any collaboration or joint venture 'except collaborating with other producers in the ordinary course of business on specific film projects'. Human resources: 28 full-time employees on roll as on June 2026 (Accounts and Finance 5, Admin 12, Business Development 8 including Executive Directors, IT 1, Compliance 1, HR 1), with approximately 150-300 skilled professionals and unskilled labour engaged per project over the production journey. Intellectual property is protected by copyright (registration optional in India) and by trademark applications: 'SUNSHINE PICTURES' application 6643047 (class 41) Accepted & Advertised, 6643048 (class 43) Abandoned, 6643049 (class 41) Objected, 6643050 (class 43) Abandoned, all applied September 26, 2024; and seven device-mark applications dated July 15, 2026 (7120962, 7120964, 7120967, 7120968, 7120969 - formalities check pass; 7120963, 7120965 - objected), all class 41. The Company also states it has no outstanding export obligations.

concerns_observed: Earnings and cash moved in opposite directions in Fiscal 2026: Net cash used in operating activities was ₹(3,320.63) lakhs against PAT of ₹4,002.24 lakhs, after CFO of ₹2,847.30 lakhs (Fiscal 2025) and ₹3,159.64 lakhs (Fiscal 2024). The Company attributes the swing to an inventory build of ₹(5,098.46) lakhs and trade receivables of ₹(3,780.97) lakhs, with net income tax paid of ₹(867.03) lakhs. Cash and cash equivalents fell to ₹48.25 lakhs at March 31, 2026 from ₹1,164.15 lakhs a year earlier, and CFI was positive ₹2,594.48 lakhs mainly on sale of investments of ₹3,049.12 lakhs. The RHP carries this as its own risk factor RF 8.

The margin step-up sits in the inventory line, not in trading performance. The Operational Cost note prints, for Fiscal 2026: Opening Stock of Media Content (including Under Production) ₹2,407.56 lakhs, Add Cost Incurred during the year ₹6,460.96 lakhs, less Closing Stock ₹(7,506.02) lakhs, giving Operational Cost of ₹1,362.50 lakhs. The comparatives are Operational Cost ₹5,097.53 lakhs (Fiscal 2025) and ₹6,223.63 lakhs (Fiscal 2024) on closing stock of ₹2,407.56 lakhs and ₹2,431.68 lakhs. EBITDA Margin printed at 78.65% for Fiscal 2026 against 49.12% and 55.29%. Whether Fiscal 2026 margin is repeatable therefore depends entirely on how the ₹7,506.02 lakhs of capitalised content is ultimately monetised and expensed.

The three-year trend is not like-for-like. Fiscal 2026 is presented on a STANDALONE basis while Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024 are CONSOLIDATED — the statement headers, the cash-flow notes and the contingent-liability table all say so. The RHP's own KPI table compounds this: its column headers read 2026 (Standalone), 2025 (Consolidated), 2024 (Consolidated) while the note immediately below states that the financial figures for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 are based on consolidated financials. Every growth, margin and days comparison in the document, including the (27.96)% and (22.77)% revenue declines, crosses that basis change.

Working capital has swollen past the size of the business. Net working capital was ₹12,646.25 lakhs at March 31, 2026, stated as 169.89% of revenue from operations, against ₹7,298.19 lakhs (70.63%) at March 31, 2025 and ₹5,103.24 lakhs (38.14%) at March 31, 2024. Holding days printed by the Company: inventory 119 (Fiscal 2024), 173 (Fiscal 2025), 1,328 (Fiscal 2026); trade receivables 11, 64, 233; trade payables 29, 42, 34. Trade receivables of ₹6,650.54 lakhs and inventories of ₹7,506.02 lakhs at March 31, 2026 compare with revenue from operations of ₹7,443.67 lakhs for the same year. Management describes the 1,328 inventory days as purely a mathematical outcome of the formula and not slow-moving, obsolete or unsaleable stock.

The Fiscal 2027 working-capital plan assumes all three cycles reverse at once. The estimate takes trade receivables from 233 days to 117, inventory from 1,328 days to 314 and trade payables from 34 days to 11, with estimated inventories still rising to ₹18,304.31 lakhs and other current assets to ₹7,351.39 lakhs within a Total Working Capital Requirement of ₹32,049.37 lakhs. The reversal is stated to be contingent on the release and monetisation of Governor: The Silent Saviour (released June 12, 2026) and Hisaab (expected Q2 Fiscal 2027), and the estimate itself is stated to use assumptions about future events and management actions that are not necessarily expected to occur.

The only quantified object of the Fresh Issue is working capital of up to ₹11,250.00 lakhs, against the Company's own stated Fiscal 2027 requirement of ₹32,049.37 lakhs; General Corporate Purposes is printed as [●] and is capped at 25% of Gross Proceeds. The RHP states the deployment has not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency, resting instead on management estimates of future financial performance approved by Board resolution dated July 27, 2026 and certified by the statutory auditor. There is no supplier, contract, purchase order or quotation behind any part of it — this is not a capex issue, so there is no execution schedule to test against.

The auditor's Emphasis of Matter goes to the timing of Fiscal 2026 revenue. The examination report records that the assignment agreement with Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited dated March 27, 2026, granting OTT release rights for The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond with effect from that date, was executed inside an eight-week theatrical holdback running from the first theatrical release of February 27, 2026, and was not in prima facie alignment with that holdback arrangement. The revenue was recognised in Fiscal 2025-26 under Ind AS 115. Management represents the OTT release actually occurred on May 1, 2026, after the holdback expired, and the auditor's opinion is not modified. The RHP prints no discrete amount for the transaction. The risk-factor chapter carries the matter as an orphaned paragraph at the end of RF 57, its heading missing.

Revenue is hit-dependent and customer-concentrated, and the customers are unnamed. The Kerala Story alone contributed ₹14,704.18 lakhs of cumulative revenue against Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations of ₹7,443.67 lakhs. Customer concentration (₹ lakhs / % of total revenue): top 1 — Fiscal 2026 2,000.00 (26.87%), Fiscal 2025 4,950.00 (47.90%), Fiscal 2024 3,824.60 (28.58%); top 5 — 5,568.60 (74.81%), 10,315.59 (99.83%), 11,117.33 (83.09%); top 10 — 6,532.31 (87.76%), 10,330.92 (99.98%), 13,085.60 (97.80%). The RHP states it is unable to disclose the names of these customers due to non-receipt of their consent, so counterparty credit quality cannot be assessed from the document.

A criminal prosecution by the Registrar of Companies is live against the Company AND both senior Promoters, and its next hearing falls after the Offer. Miscellaneous application 687/MISC/2025 was filed by the Assistant Registrar of Companies, Maharashtra, Mumbai before the Metropolitan Magistrate, 40th Court, Girgaon, Mumbai against Sunshine Pictures Limited (Accused 1), Vipul Amrutlal Shah (Accused 2), Shefali Vipul Shah (Accused 3), Anil S. Masand (Accused 4) and Yogita G. Patil (Accused 5), alleging contravention of Sections 129(7), 128(6), 450 and 143(15) of the Companies Act, 2013 and Section 127(2) of the Companies Act, 1956, over accounting treatments, provisioning and disclosures in past financial statements. It follows an inspection under Section 206(5) initiated by the Regional Director, Western Region vide notice RD(WR)/INSP/Sunshine/7673 dated February 17, 2023. The RoC has also applied under Section 473 CrPC for condonation of delay; the hearing set for March 3, 2026 stands adjourned to September 17, 2026. Exposure is printed as Not Ascertainable. The RHP is internally inconsistent on the number, citing Misc. Application No. 687 of 2024 in the risk factor and No. 687 of 2025 in the litigation chapter.

Almost the entire pre-Offer share count was created twenty months before the RHP, on top of two promoter-only share repurchases at prices unrelated to the promoters' cost. The bonus issue of December 25, 2024 in the ratio 213:1 created 2,62,25,625 of the 2,63,48,750 pre-Offer Equity Shares (Vipul Amrutlal Shah 76,19,223; Shefali Vipul Shah 65,56,353; Maurya Vipul Shah 60,23,640; Aryaman Vipul Shah 60,23,640). It was preceded by a buyback of 46,875 shares at ₹1,130 on June 3, 2020 and 17,500 shares at ₹5,707 on December 1, 2023, both from Vipul Amrutlal Shah, with a related-party outflow of ₹998.73 lakhs recorded in Fiscal 2024. Auditor-certified average cost of acquisition is ₹0.87 (Vipul Amrutlal Shah) and ₹0.44 (Shefali Vipul Shah), with the last three years weighted average at ₹0.08 and the one-year and eighteen-month columns shown as a dash. Securities Premium fell from ₹3,458.93 lakhs (Fiscal 2024) to ₹836.37 lakhs (Fiscal 2025).

Related-party dependence runs through the operating base and the funding. The Registered Office at A-102 Bharat Ark is leased from Promoter Vipul Amrutlal Shah at ₹8,00,000 per month for April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027 (rent charged ₹96.00 lakhs in Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025, ₹93.00 lakhs in Fiscal 2024), and the RHP discloses that the Promoter has in the past modified the lease deed to reduce the space allocated to the Company in order to accommodate other Promoter Group entities. Outstanding at March 31, 2026: a refundable deposit of ₹150.00 lakhs with Vipul Amrutlal Shah, stated at 0.84% of total assets, and loans and advances of ₹206.63 lakhs to Miracle Movies, a proprietary concern of a relative of a KMP, stated at 1.15% of total assets, plus a security deposit of ₹160.00 lakhs with the same party. Promoter remuneration rose to ₹300.00 lakhs (Fiscal 2026) from ₹159.17 lakhs.

The promoter loan was repriced immediately before the Offer period. The unsecured facility from Vipul Amrutlal Shah, outstanding ₹420.00 lakhs at March 31, 2026 against a sanction of ₹1,100.00 lakhs, is printed at 18% p.a. reduced to 10% p.a. with effect from October 1, 2024; interest charged was ₹57.64 lakhs (Fiscal 2026), ₹102.43 lakhs (Fiscal 2025) and ₹31.73 lakhs (Fiscal 2024). Both this facility and the ICICI Bank overdraft are repayable on demand, and the RHP's own text carries a drafting error in the covenant risk factor — a sentence reading that the Company assures investors ICICI Bank will not seek to enforce their rights, in a passage plainly intended as a negative assurance.

Statutory-dues discipline is deteriorating on the Company's own balance sheet even as the risk factor claims timeliness. The restated balance sheet carries Liability for interest and late fees on TDS and income tax of ₹3.78 lakhs (March 31, 2024), ₹26.55 lakhs (March 31, 2025) and ₹48.24 lakhs (March 31, 2026), and MD&A attributes part of the Fiscal 2025 rise in finance costs to a higher incidence of interest on statutory dues — while the statutory-dues risk factor states timely payment of GST, professional tax, ESI and provident fund for the last three fiscals. The Certificate on Defaults and Non-Payment of Statutory Dues dated July 27, 2026 is listed for inspection but its contents are not reproduced.

Contingent exposure is concentrated in two old tax matters and is large relative to net worth: other money for which the Company is contingently liable ₹3,172.96 lakhs (Fiscal 2026 standalone), ₹3,172.91 lakhs (Fiscal 2025 consolidated), ₹1,290.27 lakhs (Fiscal 2024 consolidated), against Net Worth of ₹14,513.46 lakhs. The components are an income tax order of ₹1,882.19 lakhs dated March 7, 2025 under section 147 r.w.s. 144 for AY 2020-21 (appealed under section 246A) and a service tax demand and penalty of ₹1,290.27 lakhs dated March 16, 2018 by the Commissioner CGST Mumbai West for April 2011 to March 2015 (appealed under section 86(1) of the Finance Act, 1994), plus ₹0.50 lakhs and ₹0.06 lakhs under section 154. The RHP separately shows direct and indirect tax proceedings against the Company at ₹3,174.42 lakhs across 8 matters — the same matters under a second head, not additional exposure.

This Red Herring Prospectus does not price the Offer. The Price Band, Offer Price, Floor Price, Cap Price, the aggregate Fresh Issue and Offer for Sale amounts, Gross Proceeds, Offer expenses, Net Proceeds, the percentage of Net Proceeds per object, post-Offer capital, post-Offer promoter holding, the entire lock-in table and the Company's own P/E ratio are all printed as [●], to be advertised separately two working days before the Offer opens. No valuation conclusion can be drawn from this document. The peer P/Es it prints — 81.00 (Panorama Studios International), 8.68 (Baweja Studios), NA (Balaji Telefilms, loss-making), and an Industry Composite of 44.84 — belong to those peers, computed on their closing prices as on July 24, 2026, and are not this issuer's multiple.

The Offer for Sale is entirely by the two senior Promoters — Vipul Amrutlal Shah up to 20,31,388 Equity Shares (66.88% of the offered shares) and Shefali Vipul Shah up to 10,05,769 (33.12%) — out of a combined pre-Offer holding of 1,42,42,128 shares, 54.05% of pre-Offer capital. The Company receives no part of those proceeds. Set against average acquisition costs of ₹0.87 and ₹0.44, the OFS is the promoters' first realisation event at a market-set price.

Revenue has fallen for two consecutive years and the mix is unstable: revenue from operations ₹13,379.80 lakhs (Fiscal 2024), ₹10,333.01 lakhs (Fiscal 2025), ₹7,443.67 lakhs (Fiscal 2026), with printed growth of 404.72%, (22.77)% and (27.96)%. The product split swings just as hard — films 97.78%, 52.08%, 89.68%; web series and TV serials 2.06%, 47.90%, 1.32%; others 0.16%, 0.02%, 8.99% — and the sole-produced versus co-produced split moves from 99.83%/nil (Fiscal 2024) to 78.60%/21.38% (Fiscal 2025) to 90.00%/nil (Fiscal 2026). No two consecutive years are driven by the same thing.

Operational control over the means of production is thin and partly committed away. The Company owns equipment with an aggregate value of ₹13.00 lakhs as at March 31, 2026 and rents cameras, lights, grips and setting equipment per project (hiring cost ₹264.20 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, ₹445.64 lakhs in Fiscal 2025); it has 28 employees on roll as on June 2026 and engages heads of department who have no direct contractual relationship with it (₹1,199.51 lakhs, 18.57% of total expenses in Fiscal 2026). A reputable studio holds a right of first look over future projects for three years from November 20, 2023, and has already approved Hisaab, Samuk and Bheem into the co-production model; Zee Studios holds 100% of exploitation rights for Sanak.

Content is exposed to political and judicial challenge on the Company's two largest recent titles. Public exhibition of The Kerala Story was banned in West Bengal until the Supreme Court stayed that order (WPA(P) 230 of 2023 and 233 of 2023; SLP (C) 010391 of 2023; SLP(C) 010166/2023; Writ Petitions 15119, 15126, 15143 and 15132 of 2023), and a Single Judge of the Kerala High Court stayed release of The Kerala Story 2 in Kerala on writ petitions challenging the CBFC certification before a Division Bench stayed that order. WP (PIL) No. 49 of 2026 alleging the film defames the State of Kerala was withdrawn with liberty to file afresh on the same cause of action (order dated March 5, 2026), and WP (C) No. 11010 of 2026 involves the Promoters.

The RHP's own record-keeping shows repeated lapses: Form ADT-1 for an auditor appointment in casual vacancy dated August 24, 2022, Form MGT-14 for the Section 180(1)(a) resolution dated March 16, 2020, Form AOC-4 XBRL for FY2020, FY2022 and FY2023 and Form MGT-7 for FY2022 and FY2024 were all filed late with additional fees; annexures to the FY2022-23 Board Report were not attached; a charge against an overdraft facility was not registered in FY2022-23 and the RHP does not state whether it was subsequently registered. The statutory auditor changed twice in three years (Sunil Karda resigned August 14, 2024; M/s Satyanarayan Goyal & Co. LLP appointed August 21, 2024), and the Company holds no appointment, resignation or experience letters for Independent Director Paresh Ganatra, relying on an FIR dated November 29, 2024 for their loss.

The Book Running Lead Manager is doing only its second Main Board issue: the RHP states GYR Capital Advisors Private Limited has previously completed one public issue on the Main Board and warns that any deficiency, delay or inefficiency by the BRLM may affect the timing, investor participation, pricing or overall success of the Offer. Trade receivables of ₹300 lakhs, 4.51% of total trade receivables, were outstanding beyond six months from their due dates at March 31, 2026.

Financial information of the sole Group Company, De Novo Cinematics Private Limited — reserves, sales, profit or loss after tax, EPS, diluted EPS and NAV for the last three fiscals — is not in the RHP; it is hosted on the Company's website and expressly stated not to form part of the RHP.

strengths_observed: Printed profitability is high on every measure the RHP states for Fiscal 2026: EBITDA ₹5,854.81 lakhs at an EBITDA Margin of 78.65% (49.12% in Fiscal 2025, 55.29% in Fiscal 2024), Operating EBITDA ₹5,702.55 lakhs at 76.61%, PAT ₹4,002.24 lakhs at a PAT Margin of 53.77%, Basic and Diluted EPS ₹15.19, RoNW 27.58%, RoE 31.99% and RoCE 36.20%. Against the RHP's own peer set for the same fiscal, peer EBITDA Margins print at 10.50% (Panorama Studios International), 17.51% (Baweja Studios) and (25.08)% (Balaji Telefilms). Note the composition point recorded under concerns: the Operational Cost note prints Cost Incurred during the year ₹6,460.96 lakhs against Closing Stock of Media Content (including Under Production) ₹7,506.02 lakhs, leaving Operational Cost of ₹1,362.50 lakhs (Fiscal 2025: ₹5,097.53 lakhs; Fiscal 2024: ₹6,223.63 lakhs).

The balance sheet carries little external debt and no pledged promoter shares: Net Worth ₹14,513.46 lakhs (Fiscal 2025 ₹10,506.88 lakhs, Fiscal 2024 ₹7,059.63 lakhs) against Total Borrowings of ₹909.42 lakhs, comprising an ICICI Bank dropline overdraft of ₹271.16 lakhs (sanctioned ₹820.00 lakhs on June 14, 2022, priced at Repo Rate plus a spread of 3.15% p.a.), an ICICI Bank vehicle term loan of ₹218.26 lakhs at 8.90% with 44 instalments of ₹5,83,201 outstanding, and the promoter loan of ₹420.00 lakhs. The RHP states none of the Equity Shares held by the Promoters is pledged and that all promoter holdings are dematerialised. NAV per Equity Share as at March 31, 2026 is ₹55.08.

The forward slate is named, dated and attached to identifiable counterparties rather than described generically: Hisaab, co-produced with Jio Studios, has completed principal photography and is in post-production for a Fiscal 2027 release; Nanavati vs Nanavati is a web series produced for Amazon Seller Services Private Limited with principal photography scheduled to commence July 20, 2026; Samuk is a sole production with photography scheduled from August 2026 and a Fiscal 2027 release; six films and two web series sit in the disclosed pipeline (Kaanha, Fevicol, Buldozer, Good Morning Rhea, Bheem, Maaya, Nanavati vs Nanavati Season 2 and The Kerala Story 3). Governor: The Silent Saviour was released June 12, 2026, after the Fiscal 2026 balance sheet date. The RHP attaches no value to any pipeline title.

The seventeen-year production record is quantified title by title, auditor-certified: Contribution to Company's Revenue (₹ in lakhs) The Kerala Story 14,704.18; Holiday: A Soldier is Never Off Duty 9,086.02; Bhed Bharam TV serial 4,950.00; Action Replayy 4,556.63; Humans web series 4,257.40; Sanak 4,143.35; The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond 3,970.85; Commando web series 2,803.34; Bastar 2,616.67; Force 2,446.56; Commando 2 2,368.45; Commando: One Man Army 1,613.28; Pukaar 1,575.00; Force 2 677.03; Commando 3 666.28; Bhai Bhaiya aur Brother 427.50; Kuch Love Jaisa 420.49; Happy Birthday Mummy Ji 30.00 (certified by M/s. Piyush Kothari & Associates, certificate dated July 27, 2026). Thirteen commercial films, two web series, three TV serials and one short film produced as on the date of the RHP.

Monitoring of the Fresh Issue is stronger than the regulatory minimum on one axis: CARE Ratings Limited (SEBI registration IN/CRA/004/1999) has been appointed as Monitoring Agency under a Monitoring Agency Agreement dated August 26, 2025, and the RHP states the mandate covers the Gross Proceeds, not merely the Net Proceeds, with quarterly reporting to the Audit Committee under Regulations 18(3) and 32(3) of the SEBI Listing Regulations and an annual statement of funds used for other purposes certified by the statutory auditor. The RHP also confirms no part of the Gross Proceeds will go to Promoters, Promoter Group, Directors, Group Companies or KMPs, and that Offer proceeds will not repay promoter loans.

The Bhed Bharam contract shows completed delivery rather than an open commitment: the RHP states all 150 contracted episodes were delivered and total revenue of ₹4,950.00 lakhs was billed to Prasar Bharati, Doordarshan, and that TRP performance will not affect the present contract. Export revenue rose to 13.45% of total revenue in Fiscal 2026 from 0.04% in Fiscal 2025 and 3.20% in Fiscal 2024.

The Board is eight strong with four Non-Executive Independent Directors, including Manmohan Ramanna Shetty (founder of Adlabs Films Limited, former Chairman of the National Film Development Corporation, over 31 years in the industry) and Kapil Bagla (over 21 years across financial services, investment banking and media). Audit and Nomination and Remuneration Committees were constituted September 30, 2024 and re-constituted April 24, 2026, with the Audit Committee chaired by a Chartered Accountant, Pawan S Bachani.

The stated co-production construct de-risks individual titles on the Company's own description: a fixed production fee with a contractually assured minimum consideration regardless of box-office outcome plus a share of intellectual property and profits beyond a threshold, and the D&B Report states exposure to any individual project is limited to 30% of the total annual budget. Contingent claims against the Company not acknowledged as debt are nil in all three fiscals and guarantees excluding financial guarantees are nil; total insurance coverage as of July 24, 2026 was ₹118,45,86,037, stated as 0.82 times the net assets of the Company.

Working capital funding for Fiscal 2027 is planned without new borrowing: the Sources of Finance rows print Borrowings for working capital requirements as nil, Total Equity/Internal Accruals ₹20,799.37 lakhs and Proceeds from the Offer ₹11,250.00 lakhs against a Total Working Capital Requirement of ₹32,049.37 lakhs. Historical borrowings in the same table fell from ₹1,666.82 lakhs (Fiscal 2024) to ₹849.73 lakhs (Fiscal 2025) to ₹691.16 lakhs (Fiscal 2026).
